scope: All27 grammar lesson groups/29 grammar topics, source references and four practical-language banks. This is a curriculum/source audit; final saved-PDF review is still root release work.
principle: Main lessons introduce language in context; grammar reference organizes the complete taught A1 system and makes relevant forms usable for self-study. It need not add unrelated grammar simply to have more items. Vocabulary breadth and grammar-system completeness are different checks.

groups.judgment: Seven subjects, positive/negative/yes-no questions, insertion/inversion and short answers make the bank a fuller organized system than the contextual main examples.
Sound-based a/an plus complete seven-subject affirmative contraction table extends the main examples. No need to import advanced article uses.
Capitalization reference is appropriate and substantive, but the main lesson lacked its link. Added Go-to Grammar—Capital letters p79 beside the main focus.
Near/far and singular/plural supply all four taught demonstrative combinations. The full reference may reuse those four core forms; new tasks supply consolidation.
First mention versus known item is explicitly aligned for both a/an. Core article meaning is complete for this A1 stage; broader article idioms are not required.
One owner, name ending in s and plural owner apostrophes are explicitly contrasted. All taught forms are covered; irregular plural ownership would be optional extension, not a missing assessed form.
Before-noun and after-be positions plus unchanged plural adjective are clear. Adjective order must not be added as unrelated extension.
Reference consolidates positive third-person -s/-es/has. The separate3B bank correctly owns negative/question forms; merging later material into3A would blur progression.
Positive/negative/question/short-answer paradigm, full/short negatives, do/does base-verb correction and be-versus-action contrast form a usable reference.
Four taught question words are mapped to answer types and full question/answer models. Additional why/how language is not needed solely to make a bigger grammar list.
Frequency placement before action verbs and after be is visible; before/after is anchored to ordered events and both noun/clause models. Complete taught concept scope is retained.

Visual singular/plural/countable-versus-uncountable contrast, articles and no-plural examples support the introduced system. Vocabulary breadth belongs in the food bank rather than extra grammar topics.
All seven subject/object pronoun pairs and noun-to-pronoun full models are available; this is legitimate full-system consolidation even though main has the complete pronoun set.
Main had fuller countable/uncountable coverage. Added aligned not-enough tomatoes/oil models so the bank explicitly includes not enough with uncountable nouns, using taught vocabulary.
Reason/result arrows and reordered because/so clauses plus punctuation repair form an appropriate writing reference; no new connectors are needed for a quota.
Added three clear yes/no short-answer pairs and a full What-question/answer model. They were in the main lesson and relevant to the existing bank tasks but absent from its reference.
Picture-supported too small/not big enough/big enough contrast already makes adjective position and meaning clear; no extra grammar topic needed.
Expanded the week-only reference to a native chart of every/once/twice/three times across day/week/month/year. The earlier bank was narrower than its own main lesson.

All six taught prepositions have distinct photographic models and clear captions. Adding behind/between could be optional vocabulary expansion with new pictures, not required to repair the taught grammar system.
Restored along/across/through to the reference beside the existing streets/crosswalks/park-path picture; retained route tasks and orientation.
Core can/cannot/cant/question/base-verb reference was sound; added one compact relevant question plus positive/negative short answers already taught in the main lesson.
Was/were subject groups, negatives, questions and short answers form a complete bounded system; today/yesterday evidence supports the tasks.
In-month/in-year/on-date and ago timeline are explicitly structured. Ordinal vocabulary is covered in the separate word bank; no tense expansion is required.
Regular past positive/negative/question forms, did-versus-was distinction and -ed spelling variants are present; a short-answer model supports the productive question task.

Trip picture, regular/irregular positive forms and did+base negative/question pattern consolidate the introduced past travel system. Other known travel verbs are retrieved in tasks and the lexical bank; no new past tense is needed.
Added the main lessons relevant should-question and yes/no short answers compactly. Existing advice meanings and base-verb repair remain.
Have/has and singular/plural hurts/hurt plus a useful change-of-plan message cover this limited health grammar scope; diagnostic language or new question tenses are unnecessary.

practical_banks.judgment: Full ask/choose/pay/check exchange with receipt repair and private customer/shopkeeper notes. Useful functional expansion, not an extra tense.
Map/opening evidence, visitor needs and route/check task extend can/directions productively. Opposite has an explicit model; all taught grammar need not be repeated.
Complete diary source, sequencing, repair and open writing. Irregular lexical forms live in the vocabulary bank; no excluded verb-list annex is needed.
Question/clarification/confirmation models and booking repair/role play complete the functional scope. Return to main8D works through its linked code heading.
